title: Insurance By Distance
summary:
Asia's oil diversification drive can redraw global tanker routes
For many decades, mapping the oil flows in Asia was simple. The largest consumers in the region, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and later, China and India had limited or no domestic crude oil production. At the same time, the Middle East, which was geographically fairly close, had abundant resources.
